quote.text: “It is difficult to get a man to understand something when his salary depends upon his not understanding it.”
quote.author: Upton Sinclair, I, Candidate for Governor: And How I Got Licked (1935)

stories.kicker: The Gulf · The war returns to the water
stories.headline: Tanker for tanker
stories.dek: After a month’s lull, Washington sinks Iranian tankers in reprisal — a doctrine, not an incident. Tehran hits back, names a “restricted zone,” and Brent still sits near ninety-five. The market is pricing a bounded war.

stories.headline: Hot jobs flip the Fed toward a hike
stories.dek: August payrolls came in triple the forecast, and rate-hike odds swung back toward sixty per cent under a hawkish Warsh Fed. The dominant force is rates; the odd one out is gold, climbing anyway.

stories.kicker: Down the rabbit hole · Gravel cycling
stories.headline: One bike to do everything
stories.dek: A drop-bar bike built for the space between road and mountain — the gnarmac. It sold itself as escape and inclusion; then it grew a twelve-thousand-dollar arms race. This is the descent.

stories.kicker: The air, and the growth call
stories.headline: The sky clears; the pressure doesn’t
stories.dek: The first unhealthy air since 2023 eased over the weekend — on the wind, not on the diplomacy. And the forecasters lifted the growth call to five per cent while naming the thing that could break it.

stories.kicker: Buy it once · The everyday-carry knife
stories.headline: Four systems, one tool for life
stories.dek: A folding knife is steel, lock, handle and pivot — judge those and you can price any knife cold. The catch, for a Singapore reader, is that this is a category to collect and travel with, not to carry.

stories.kicker: The frontier · The densest week of the year
stories.headline: Three frontier launches, and a breach in the rear-view
stories.dek: OpenAI ships the first model it says crossed its critical-cyber line — in the same seventy-two hours as new frontier models from Google and Anthropic. The safeguards are being sold as the product.

stories.kicker: Gear we’re watching · The face computer
stories.headline: Everything but a price
stories.dek: XREAL’s Aura turned up at IFA with a seventy-degree see-through display, a Bose-tuned soundstage and a pocket puck — undercutting Snap by roughly seven hundred dollars. The catch is the wire, and a number XREAL still won’t commit to.

stories.headline: Zenith drops the chronograph, keeps the El Primero
stories.dek: At Geneva Watch Days, Zenith took its famous high-frequency movement, threw away the stopwatch, and built a clean two-hundred-metre sports watch around it. The most-talked-about accessible-luxury release of the show — and a genuine provocation.

stories.headline: Spider-Man owns Labor Day — and the ledger
stories.dek: Six weekends in, “Brand New Day” is still number one, the fastest film ever to nine hundred million domestic, and past two billion worldwide. Meanwhile, Venice keeps its Lion in its pocket until Saturday.

stories.kicker: Raising them well · The feed, and the floor
stories.headline: Singapore moves the goalposts on kids and the feed
stories.dek: “I’m over thirteen” is “just not good enough,” the Prime Minister said. Mandatory age assurance is coming — landing exactly as a twelve-year-old enters Secondary One.

stories.kicker: The long game · The dose that matters
stories.headline: How much lifting you actually need
stories.dek: A hundred-and-forty-seven-thousand-person, thirty-year analysis pins the strength-training sweet spot at ninety to a hundred and twenty minutes a week — after which the mortality curve flattens.

stories.kicker: What’s worth booking · The dated agenda
stories.headline: Book this week, plan the season
stories.dek: One sale opens Friday and is the most time-sensitive item on the page. The rest is the season worth planning — verified, this week, against the official ticketers.

stories.headline: The con that became a confession
stories.dek: In the Philippines, a word born from a street swindle has been reforged into a national joke about spending you cannot afford. “Na-budol ako” — I got budol’d — is how a whole generation narrates surrender to the livestream.
